answer.rationale: Write-path p99 has been climbing for 90 minutes under daily settlement peak and heavy writes, which looks like saturation/queueing rather than a step-change defect. memory_b3 is the closest prior (headroom kept queue depth flat through a peak) and adding capacity does not drop customer writes. That case was provisioned before the peak, so transfer to a mid-peak add is uncertain—verify b3 before committing. A 2h-old release remains a competing cause (b1) but the trajectory fits load; skip circuit breakers because failing fast would lose writes; failover and read-replica routing lack a regional or report-query signal here.
